name: cortexagent-commands
generator: manager-assembled from agent-built bank-part1.json (phases 0-4) + bank-part2.json (phases 5-8) + wireless Phase 9 tools (manager-authored from the playbook's Phase 9 card and notes/research-wireless.md). Source-line conventions per command: 'Rahalkar Lnnn' / 'Harpreet Lnnn' point into the extracted source-book corpus; 'playbook Phase 9 card' points into books/kali-tools-commands.md; 2026-10-06 appended documented community tools (29 phase 1 OSINT/web-recon, 1 phase 5, 10 phase 6 web-attack, 1 phase 8) — dataset in integrate_new_tools.py; three Burp-suite-only candidates excluded (param-miner, turbo-intruder, inql)
sources: Harpreet Singh, Infrastructure Attack Strategies for Ethical Hacking (2024)
Claudia Lanza, Ransomware Analysis, Knowledge Extraction and Structuring (2025)
Wireless phase: aircrack-ng suite docs + hcxdumptool/hcxtools manuals as installed on this host; see notes/research-wireless.md - research-grounded, NOT from the three books

placeholder_grammar.IP: the target host's address (lab victim or scan target)
placeholder_grammar.LHOST: YOUR attacking/lab host's own address - reverse shells, spoofers and backdoors must call home here; DIFFERENT slot from {{IP}}
placeholder_grammar.IFACE: a wireless interface in managed mode (e.g. wlan0), BEFORE monitor conversion
placeholder_grammar.IFACE_MON: the monitor-mode interface airmon-ng created (typically wlan0mon)
placeholder_grammar.MAC: a client station's MAC address (use YOUR OWN lab client in deauth)
placeholder_grammar.PASSPHRASE: the lab AP's WPA2 passphrase - one you set yourself; in the decrypt step it is the recovered value
placeholder_grammar.DOMAIN: a domain or hostname you control in the lab (DNS/URL slots)
placeholder_grammar.URL: a web URL (also a prompt-reply slot for SET)
placeholder_grammar.PATH: a file path on whichever host the command runs on
placeholder_grammar.WORDLIST: a wordlist file path you built (crunch output, lab lists)
placeholder_grammar.USER: a username/account name (lab-built, never a real person)
placeholder_grammar.NUM: a count, interval or id (deauth frame count stays <= 5 in the lab)
placeholder_grammar.EMAIL: an email address (lab account only, e.g. labuser@lab.example)
placeholder_grammar.PHONE: a phone number in international format (lab fake, e.g. +15550001000)
placeholder_grammar.CODE: a country calling code without the + sign (e.g. 44)
placeholder_grammar.QUERY: a search-query string (search-engine quotes included as in the docs)
placeholder_grammar.INFILE: a local input file your lab tooling reads (a list, dump or capture)
placeholder_grammar.HOSTLIST: a local file with one target host/URL per line
placeholder_grammar.DOMAINLIST: a local file with one domain per line
placeholder_grammar.URLLIST: a local file with one URL per line
placeholder_grammar.FILE: a single local file path in your lab workspace
placeholder_grammar.JWT: a JSON Web Token — the lab sample is a three-part signed token
placeholder_grammar.CLAIM: a JWT claim (JSON) field name to modify, e.g. sub
placeholder_grammar.SECRET: the JWT's HMAC signing secret string (a lab-only secret)
placeholder_grammar.KEY: a signing/verification key (file path for a lab PEM key)
placeholder_grammar.VALUE: a generic string value used by the documented option
placeholder_grammar.CANARY: the expected-response marker used to detect blind injection
placeholder_grammar.GAIA: a Google/YouTube account's numeric Gaia identifier (lab placeholder)
placeholder_grammar.COMPANY: a company/organization name to enumerate against (lab placeholder)
placeholder_grammar.PROXY: a proxy URL:port for the tool to route through (lab listener)
placeholder_grammar.MARKUP: a parameter placeholder markup string, exactly as the tool expects
placeholder_grammar.VHOST: a virtual-host name to smuggle requests under (lab domain)
placeholder_grammar.SERVER: an outbound-interaction server URL:port the tool registers with
placeholder_grammar.ROUTES: an API-routes wordlist (.kite built by kr kb, or its JSON source)
placeholder_grammar.TIME_BUDGET: seconds the fuzzing phase may run
placeholder_grammar.MAXLEN: maximum secret length for brute-force mode
placeholder_grammar.PAYLOAD: a ysoserial gadget-chain payload class name
placeholder_grammar.COMMAND: a shell command string executed by the gadget on the lab target
placeholder_grammar.REQFILE: a raw HTTP request file (one request captured in the lab)
placeholder_grammar.PATTERN: a named gf pattern stored in ~/.gf/<name>.txt
placeholder_grammar.REGEX: a regular expression the pattern matches URLs with
placeholder_grammar.HASHTAG: a social-media hashtag without the # prefix (lab tag)
placeholder_grammar.HANDLE: a platform handle / channel name without the @ prefix
placeholder_grammar.GRAPHQL_URL: a lab GraphQL endpoint URL (e.g. http://...:4000/graphql)
placeholder_grammar.BASE_URL: a lab web-app base URL without the endpoint path
placeholder_grammar.TRUSTED: the trusted domain the JWT attack targets (lab domain)
placeholder_grammar.USER1: a first username to search (lab placeholder)
placeholder_grammar.USER2: a second username to cross-search against USER1

lab_only: Every command is lab-scoped: run only against hardware, virtual machines, access points and domains you own or that are formally sanctioned. The build process never executed any of these commands; they are documentation for CortexAgent to instantiate with slip-in variables.
usage_for_cortexagent: Load tools[].commands[].cmd, replace each {{TOKEN}} slot with a lab value, keep single-quoted msfconsole -q -x batches intact (a fresh console drops module state), and cite the command's source field when provenance is requested.

host_facts: Live verification 2026-10-06 ran on Parrot Security 7.3 (echo), the playbook owner's local install - the same Debian package ecosystem as Kali. Verified live: nmap 7.95, msf 6.5.4, setoolkit 8.0.3, bettercap 2.41.7, hashcat 6.2.6, aircrack-ng suite 1.7, hcxdumptool + hcxpcapngtool 6.3.5. Absent but installable: amass, routersploit, exploitdb, openvas/gvm, evilginx2 (all confirmed in the apt index; sparta is NOT - use upstream tarball). sherlock's entrypoint is /usr/bin/sherlock.
